constants.$comment: EVERY constant this course will touch, with its status. DECLARED means the engine states it and nothing in this package derives it. EXPORTED means the engine exports it by name, so the export and the behaviour can be compared. DERIVED means this package reaches it a second way. PINNED means it is MEASURED out of the engine's behaviour and compared against a literal in digest section 3, which is a THIRD location, and against the golden's heldConstants block, which is a FOURTH. HELD means no source for it exists in this repository and it is NEVER GRADED. In FC9 almost everything is HELD and PINNED at once, which is the defining fact about this engine: a paired battery moved fifteen of seventeen constants in the engine AND the oracle together and left the suite green, because a constant that lives in two files cannot be validated by comparing those two files.
constants.0.0031 and 1.4: the two constants of the CO2 fugacity coefficient. HELD and PINNED. MEASURED in digest section 3 because log10 of the coefficient divided by the pressure is linear in the reciprocal temperature, so 20 C and 180 C at 10 bar solve for both. NEVER GRADED.
constants.250: the pressure above which the fugacity coefficient is held flat, bar. HELD, EXPORTED as FUGACITY_CAP_BAR, and PINNED by bisecting the pressure at which the coefficient stops moving. What the correlation does above it is held too, and the engine now REPORTS the cap through pressureCapApplied and a note rather than applying it in silence. NEVER GRADED, and no graded capstone field sits above it.
constants.4.93, 1119 and 0.58: the three constants of the de Waard-Milliams reaction term. HELD and PINNED: log10 of the reaction rate is linear in the reciprocal temperature and in log10 of the fugacity, so three points solve for all three. NEVER GRADED.
constants.2.45, 0.8 and 0.2: the coefficient and the two exponents of the mass-transfer term. HELD and PINNED by the doubling ratios in velocity and in diameter, plus the unit call. The exponent of the FUGACITY in the same term is exactly 1, which is a DERIVED property rather than a typed constant and is pinned as such. NEVER GRADED.
constants.2400, 0.6 and 6.7: the three constants of the protective-scale factor. HELD and PINNED, measured at 150 C and 200 C WHERE THE FACTOR IS UNCLAMPED, which is the trap: below the onset the engine returns exactly 1 and every slope measured there is zero. The generator carries a negative control proving that. NEVER GRADED.
constants.the film onset temperature: DERIVED and EXPORTED as scaleOnsetTC, computed from the correlation rather than quoted, and it MOVES with fugacity: across the seven fugacities in digest section 6 it moves by more than sixty degrees. The PUBLISHED onset is HELD and no round number is quoted anywhere. The old docstring's 60 C was never the onset.
constants.whether the scale factor multiplies the: HELD, and the most consequential held item in the module. The engine forms the series combination FIRST and then multiplies, so it applies a protective-film correction to a rate mass transfer may be controlling. The two placements give materially different answers whenever mass transfer controls. NEVER GRADED, and CLEARED BY IDENTITY in all three capstones: every scenario is below its own computed onset so its factor is exactly 1, and multiplying by 1 in either place gives the same double.
constants.-0.5 and 4: the pH correction's slope and its reference pH. Both HELD, the reference EXPORTED as PH_REFERENCE, both PINNED: the slope from the factor at pH 5 and pH 7, the reference by bisecting the pH at which the engine stops returning a factor. The ONE DECADE PER TWO pH UNITS property is DERIVED and is constant-free. What the correlation does BELOW the reference is HELD, and the engine REFUSES there rather than returning 1. NEVER GRADED.
constants.0.0035: the H2S partial pressure screening threshold, bar. HELD, EXPORTED as SOUR_THRESHOLD_BAR, PINNED by bisecting the sour flag. KEPT UNCHANGED on purpose: moving a live number without a source would repeat the original mistake inverted. NEVER GRADED, and no graded field compares anything against it.
constants.14.503773800721815: bar to psia. EXPORTED as BAR_TO_PSIA. It is a ROUNDED conversion: rebuilt from the definitions of the bar and the pound-force it is 14.503773773020923, and the engine's value sits 1.910e-9 above that. The engine comment says so at engines 5cbdca5, and the value is kept because it moves nothing graded. PINNED from the psia the engine reports for a 1 bar partial pressure. SOUR_THRESHOLD_PSIA is DERIVED from it and is 0.050763208302526355 psia, which is NOT 0.05; the gate asserts it is not 0.05. GRADEABLE, and one Associate field uses it.
constants.1/500 and 1/20: the H2S to CO2 ratio boundaries. Both HELD, both EXPORTED, both PINNED by bisecting the regime WORD. The RATIO itself is DERIVED and pressure free, and that is what makes it gradeable while the boundaries are not: the oracle route is built from MOLE FRACTIONS so it needs no pressure at all, which is what catches a pH2S built from the total pressure or from a fugacity.
constants.100 and 50: the film-stripping and moderate wall-shear thresholds, Pa. Both HELD, both EXPORTED, both PINNED by bisecting the velocity at which the risk word turns and reading the shear there. The 100 Pa one now drives the RATE as well as a coloured word, so it matters more after the repair than before. NEVER GRADED. Two Expert fields STATE that the credit has been removed rather than deriving that it was, which is how they are cleared.
constants.0.046, -0.2 and 16: the Blasius coefficient, its exponent and the laminar constant. All HELD and PINNED from the friction factor at Reynolds 200000, 800000 and 1500. NEVER GRADED, and no graded field reads a friction factor or a wall shear. The Reynolds NUMBER itself is a DEFINITION and is gradeable.
constants.4000: the laminar to turbulent branch switch. HELD, EXPORTED as SHEAR_SWITCH_RE, PINNED by bisecting the branch NAME the engine returns. It is a GENUINE DISCONTINUITY and the digest MEASURES its size rather than describing it. It is not smoothed, because smoothing it would be a third invented correlation. NEVER GRADED.
constants.0.1, 0.5 and 1.0: the rate category bands, mm/yr. All HELD, EXPORTED as RATE_CATEGORY_BANDS, PINNED by bisecting the category WORD. The engine says in its own held list that they may be optimistic by one or two steps. NEVER GRADED, and no graded field is a band label of any kind.
constants.0.1: the inhibitor shortfall trigger, percentage points. A stated CONVENTION of the repair, EXPORTED as INHIBITOR_SHORTFALL_PP, PINNED by bisecting the availability at which the warning first appears at a 50 percent efficiency. It replaced a guard that compared the efficiency strictly against 0.9, which was switched off at the app's own default of exactly 90.
constants.0.1 as the controlling margin: the relative gap inside which the engine reports the two resistances as comparable rather than naming one. A stated REPORTING threshold and the engine says so, EXPORTED as CONTROLLING_MARGIN, PINNED by solving the velocity that puts the transport term a stated ratio above the reaction term and bisecting the word. It is not a claim about where mass transfer stops mattering.
constants.-273.15: absolute zero in degrees Celsius. A DEFINITION, and one of only four range guards this course treats as enforced rather than held: 0 to 1 on every fraction, 0 to 14 on pH, a temperature above absolute zero, and the partial-pressure sum against the total. EVERY PUBLISHED VALIDITY BAND of every correlation above is HELD and none is enforced.
constants.25.4 and 1000: millimetres per inch and mils per inch, for the mpy conversion the studio now prints beside every rate. DEFINITIONS.
constants.the studio's 14.5038, 14.7, 1.8, 32, 0.3: DECLARED by the Suite layer, not by the engine: these are the studio's own unit factors, stated in digest section 24. 14.5038 is a TRUNCATION of the engine's exported BAR_TO_PSIA, so a pressure converted through the studio and one converted through the engine's own factor differ in the sixth significant figure, and the digest MEASURES what that is worth on the shipped default rate. This is why all three capstones state their conditions in the ENGINE's units and say so: grading which rounding the app used would grade the app rather than corrosion. The others (14.7, 1.8, 32, 0.3048, 0.0254, 16.0185, 25.4, 1000) are DEFINITIONS or stated offsets.
constants.the inspection interval, the minimum thi: NOT PROVIDED, which is a stronger statement than HELD. They require a standard the module does not carry, they are in the engine's NOT_PROVIDED list, and the course teaches the word integrity narrowly: an allowance divided by a rate.
constants.an erosional velocity criterion: NOT PROVIDED, recorded in the engine's NOT_PROVIDED list, and NOT FIXED by the repair. The wall shear this module computes is for a different purpose entirely. The course CITES the Casing & Tubing Design Expert tier, which owns the criterion.
constants.the MR0175 / ISO 15156 severity region a: WITHDRAWN, not held. An invented fit, log10(pH2S / 0.0035) - (pH - 3.5), breaking at 1 and 2.5, serving three named material recommendations in a live app. The repair removed the claim rather than retuning it. The absence is DECLARED through regionProvided and materialGuidanceProvided, both false. The gate asserts the three guidance strings and the function name are absent from the source, that neither standard name appears in a LINE OF CODE, and that both names DO survive in the header comment so the record of the withdrawal is not itself erased. NEVER GRADED, and it is this course's headline lesson.

No lesson, bank, key truth or panel is written yet.
plan.thesis: A corrosion rate is a claim about a mechanism, and this engine's claim rests on eleven numbers with no source in the repository. The course therefore teaches the rate as a screening argument to be read and argued with, and grades only what the engine can stand behind: what is in the stream, how fast it moves, what the inhibitor programme actually delivers, and what the allowance actually buys.

tiers.beginner: Associate. WHAT IS IN THE STREAM, AND WHAT THE ENGINE WILL NOT SAY. Why: the bookkeeping is the only part of this module that is arithmetic over the inputs, so it is where a learner can be right for a reason they can state. It carries the withdrawal as a story, because the first thing to know about this app is what it stopped claiming.
tiers.intermediate: Professional. THE INHIBITOR PROGRAMME AND THE ALLOWANCE. Why: a 95 percent inhibitor at 80 percent availability delivers 76 percent, and that arithmetic is the one lesson the module exists to teach. It is also the only part of the engine with no correlation constant in it, so it is the only part a capstone can grade without leaning on a held number.
tiers.advanced: Expert. THE LIMITS, AND INVERSION AGAINST THEM. Why: the interesting questions are all inversions (what rate can I tolerate, what availability do I need, what allowance reinstates the design life) and all six graded fields are found by bisecting a verdict the engine returns. The tier closes on the withdrawal as a general lesson about invented authority.

capstones.beginner: OBIGBO, a high-pressure wet gas gathering line: the CO2 partial pressure, the H2S partial pressure in psia, the H2S to CO2 mole ratio, the Reynolds number, the effective inhibition and the metal-loss ratio against the datasheet figure.
capstones.intermediate: NEMBE CREEK, an oil line whose uninhibited wall-loss rate came off a two-year ultrasonic survey: the retained fraction, the shortfall in percentage points, the inhibited rate, the remaining life, the allowance the design life demands and the years the availability shortfall costs.
capstones.advanced: SOKU, a line where the wall shear has already removed the inhibitor credit: the tolerable rate, the availability a stated target protection needs, the availability the design life needs, the allowance that reinstates the design life with part of it already gone, the stripped-film life and the ratio of the two lives.
capstones.unitsRule: ALL THREE STATE THEIR CONDITIONS IN THE ENGINE'S UNITS and say so on the page. Digest section 24 is why: the studio's psig to bar factor is a truncation of the engine's exact one, the difference is large enough to fail a 5e-7 tolerance and far too small to matter to an engineer, and grading it would measure the app rather than corrosion.

digest.note: Nothing is withheld. SECTION 25 is the one section whose subject is what this engine used to do, it says so in its title and in its first line, and NOTHING FOLLOWS IT. Section 2 is about a current, permanent ABSENCE and says in its own second line that it is not repair history.

history.position: FRAMED HISTORY IS CURRICULUM, UNFRAMED HISTORY IS A DEFECT. Digest SECTION 25 is the one section whose subject is what this engine used to do. Expert m06 owns it. SECTION 2, the withdrawal, is deliberately NOT in the history section, because the absence it describes is current and permanent: its second line says so.
history.engineComments: Repair-history comment lines in the engine source are PROVENANCE. Digest section 25 COUNTS them by reading the source and states the rule it counted with, rather than quoting any of them as teaching truth.
history.framingRule: Framing comes from the HEADING above a passage or the line immediately before it. An inline prefix inside a sentence is not framing.

scopeSeams.an erosional velocity criterion: OWNED BY casingtubing (Expert M5, live), and cited again in nodal and gaswell. Associate m01 and Professional m03 CITE it and state plainly that this engine has no erosional-velocity limit and computes a wall shear for a different purpose entirely: whether an inhibitor film survives. The engine lists the absence in NOT_PROVIDED and the repair deliberately did NOT add one.
scopeSeams.wall loss taken to a derated burst press: OWNED BY torquedrag (Expert M3 and M4, live). Expert m02 cites it. This module consumes an allowance and never computes a pressure, so the comparison is a pivot.
scopeSeams.the Barlow thin-wall relation with a des: OWNED BY network (Associate M2, live). Cited by Expert m02 as the calculation that would tell you what the allowance is being taken off, which this module cannot.
scopeSeams.fugacity and partial pressure: OWNED BY fluid (Expert M1 L4, live). Associate m02 cites it for the thermodynamics and then teaches what is specific here: which quantity drives the rate, which drives the H2S threshold and the film ratio, and that no fugacity correction is applied to H2S at all.
scopeSeams.the corrosion allowance as a wall thickn: OWNED TWICE, by the Pipeline & Line Sizing studio and the Storage Tank & Venting studio, which both ADD one. This studio CONSUMES one. The wall this studio eats is not the wall either of those sized, there is no link and no minimum thickness anywhere. Recorded in digest section 21 and deliberately not wired up.
scopeSeams.corrosion, wall loss and remaining life: THE ONE PLACE THE LIVE CATALOGUE POINTS AT THIS COURSE. The integrity course (Well Integrity and P&A, DRILLING module) explicitly REFUSES all three in its own scope statement: no corrosion model, no wall loss, no remaining life. FC9 fills exactly that refusal. A lesson here may name it as the owner of barrier logic and must not borrow its vocabulary: a barrier envelope is not a corrosion allowance.
scopeSeams.what has never been taught anywhere: de Waard, Milliams, siderite, MR0175, ISO 15156, SSC, HIC, pitting, API 570, API 579, B31.G, fitness-for-service, cathodic protection, in-line inspection and non-destructive testing are at ZERO files across all live courses. This course's own ground, and the reason several of them are taught as NAMED ABSENCES rather than as content.

namingCollisions.inhibitor: LEGISLATED IN DIGEST SECTION 22. Bare 'inhibitor' already means a HYDRATE inhibitor across the flowassurance course: methanol or MEG, dosed in mass fraction of the water phase to depress a hydrate formation temperature. Here it is a CORROSION inhibitor: a filming amine with an efficiency and an availability. RULE: always write 'corrosion inhibitor' on first use in every lesson and every bank question, and never bare 'inhibitor' in a prompt, an option or a heading.
namingCollisions.erosion: LEGISLATED IN DIGEST SECTION 22. Bare 'erosion' already means a GEOLOGICAL process in the basin course: material removed from a sedimentary column over geological time. Here it would mean mechanical wall loss from solids or impingement, WHICH THIS MODULE DOES NOT MODEL AT ALL. RULE: always write 'mechanical erosion' or 'erosional wall loss', and every use must carry the statement that the engine has no erosional-velocity criterion.
namingCollisions.friction factor and Reynolds number: LEGISLATED IN DIGEST SECTION 22, and this one is a REAL DISAGREEMENT rather than a naming problem. linesizing (FC2) owns a friction factor and a Reynolds number with a different correlation and a different transition, and the two will not agree on the same pipe. The engine says so in its own docstring and the repair deliberately left the duplicate alone as a cross-module decision. RULE: always write 'the corrosion module's friction factor' or 'this module's Reynolds number', and always state that the line sizing course computes its own. Never present either as the platform's single answer.
namingCollisions.integrity: NOT A COLLISION BUT A MISREADING, and legislated in the same section. In this course 'integrity' means one arithmetic: a corrosion allowance divided by a rate. No fitness for service, no minimum thickness, no inspection interval. Say so wherever the word appears.
namingCollisions.rate: NOT A COLLISION BUT A MISREADING. The single rate is a GENERAL UNIFORM rate and the engine says so in NOT_PROVIDED. Never write it as a wall-loss prediction for a weld, a bend, a top-of-line film or a pit.

openItems.TWO FAILS-OPEN THE REPAIR LEFT IN `scree: A NEW FINDING AGAINST THE REPAIRED ENGINE, measured in digest section 17 and taught there. The FC9-0 repair's own record names the defect: `screen` used to put `shear.error` into a field and return normally, so a caller's `if (result.error)` saw nothing and the summary quietly dropped a row. It fixed the shear and reproduced the same shape one field along. (1) A BLANK or not-a-number corrosion allowance gives `life: null`, `withheld: null`, `screeningComplete: true` and NO top-level error, so the remaining-life row simply vanishes from a summary rail with nothing saying why. (2) A REFUSAL FROM `remainingLife` ARRIVES INSIDE THE `life` FIELD: an allowance already consumed past its own depth, or a negative consumed depth, returns `life: { error: ... }` with `screeningComplete: true` and no top-level error, so the refusal message never reaches anyone and `life.remainingYears` is undefined. Both are the swallowed-error class the repair named and did not remove. Not repaired here because this wave does not touch the engine; recorded, measured and TAUGHT, because a course that taught the shear order while the same shape survived one field along would teach a falsehood by omission.
openItems.a default parameter that answers a quest: `screen`'s `h2sMolFrac = 0`. A caller that OMITS the key gets a positive assertion of zero H2S: not sour, the carbonate regime, and a graded category and life. A value that is not a number refuses, and the Suite layer produces not-a-number from a blank box, so the live studio is protected by the layer above rather than by this default. `corrosionRate`'s `waterCutFrac = 1` has the same shape and points the CONSERVATIVE way. Both measured in digest sections 8 and 17. This is the class the repair removed in seven places; these two survived as default parameters.
openItems.the engine bar to psia factor is rounded: FOUND BY THE LADDER'S GO-LIVE, whose second route shares no constant with the engine. corrosion.js exports BAR_TO_PSIA = 14.503773800721815; rebuilt from the definitions (0.45359237 kg, 9.80665 m/s2, 0.0254 m, 100000 Pa) it is 14.503773773020923, so the engine sits 1.910e-9 above exact and SOUR_THRESHOLD_PSIA inherits it. The course prints both (digest section 24) and never calls it exact; grading is unaffected (3.5e-9 against a 5e-7 grade). At engines 5cbdca5 the ENGINE COMMENT says it is rounded and gives the exact value; the LITERAL IS KEPT, because changing it would move six-decimal figures in this held ladder for a 2e-9 gain.
